About Zipline

Zipline is the world’s largest and most experienced drone delivery service. We are on a mission to serve all humans equally by ensuring access to food, medicine and essential goods anytime, anywhere. We design, build, and operate the world’s largest autonomous logistics system, delivering critical supplies quickly and reliably. Today, Zipline operates on four continents, makes a delivery somewhere in the world every 30 seconds, and has completed millions of deliveries to date, including blood, vaccines, medical supplies, food, and retail products.

Our customers include the world’s largest and most prominent healthcare systems, governments, retailers, restaurants and global businesses who rely on us to save lives, reduce emissions, increase economic opportunity, and provide delivery from point A to point B as fast as possible. The drone is only 15% of what we’ve built to enable seamless, reliable, global operations.

Our system strengthens supply chains, reduces congestion, and gives people time back. With more than 140 million commercial autonomous miles safely flown, Zipline is redefining access to healthcare, consumer products, and food across the globe.

We operate at a global scale and are looking for practical problem solvers who thrive on real-world challenges and rapid growth. Our team is motivated by building systems that have a direct, meaningful impact on people’s lives and by scaling the future of logistics. We are seeking people who sculpt from first principles, enjoy facing adversity, and can do the impossible at record breaking speeds.

The Role

Does aggressively tackling cross disciplinary projects from early conceptual stages through to full field deployment sound like the way you want to spend your time? Do you eliminate circular discussions by running a test or use your hands-on skills to build a prototype instead of scheduling another meeting?

At Zipline, your work is intended for the field, where customers are counting on it every day, so there is no time for ambiguous communication or unrealistic expectations. We need dedicated engineers to burn down risk and improve reliability in our system like their life depends on it– because others' lives do. If you thrive working with a fast-paced and driven team that focuses on only the most important goals, eliminates blockers, and executes with extreme practicality, keep reading!

Materials Engineers at Zipline go deep in their area of ownership, become experts in the problem domain, and prove with testing that their system meets the rigors and edge-cases of real-world deployment. We are composed of teams that are involved with everything from the earliest designs of a new system, to creating test and validation strategies, root-causing issues with existing systems, and much more.

What You'll Do

- Materials interns can own a variety of big problems integral to our system! You can expect to:

- Perform materials characterization using tools such as section/mount/polish, optical microscopy, SEM/EDS, hardness testing, and mechanical testing.

- Support failure investigations by examining physical evidence, developing hypotheses, and identifying material or processdriven failure mechanisms.

- Evaluate the effects of manufacturing processes, surface condition, coatings, joining, and environmental exposure on component performance.

- Qualify material, supplier, or process changes through structured testing and data analysis.

- Analyze experimental data using Python, MATLAB, JMP, or similar tools and communicate conclusions through clear plots, images, and technical documentation.

- Develop or improve test methods, fixtures, procedures, and characterization workflows.

- Work cross-functionally with design, manufacturing, reliability, supplier quality, and test engineers to turn materials evidence into engineering decisions.

- Document your work so that others can easily understand key decisions made

What You'll Bring

The most critical skill we’ve seen in prior entry-level candidates is robust experience designing and actually building multiple mechanical systems outside of the classroom. This is the component of your application we’re most excited about, so please ensure that you’ve included this work in your application. Examples of things previous interns have built include submarines, solar cars in the Australian outback, electric boats and airplanes, rockets, etc.

- You’ll bring strong fundamentals in materials science and mechanical behavior for identifying material or process driven failure mechanisms.

- You have hands-on experience through research, internships, or projects involving materials characterization, mechanical testing, manufacturing, or failure analysis.

- You have experience analyzing data and clearly communicating technical conclusions.

- You must have completed at least the second year of your Undergraduate studies in Materials Science & Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Metallurgical Engineering, or a related technical field.

- Masters and PhD students are also eligible.

- You’re comfortable working independently in a laboratory environment and troubleshooting experiments.

- You're quick to change direction when you realize you’ve made a mistake OR could achieve the same goal in a simpler way

- You bias to action and communicate consistently with your team to ensure everyone is focused on meeting the project goals on time

- You can anticipate, plan and schedule your own work

- You bring a “can do” attitude, because we have a lot of vital work to get done and only work with people who are invested in solving critical problems

What Else You Should Know

Our internships are full-time positions, in-person at our South San Francisco or Dallas office. We will host this intern from January to August/September.

The hourly rate for this internship is $40 per hour. Additional benefits may include relocation support, a housing stipend, overtime pay, paid sick time, and other benefits, where applicable and subject to local requirements.

- Help evaluate performance across platforms, audiences, and content formats.

Interest in communications, marketing, social media, and/or short form video

Our goal is to push the frontier of human-robot interaction by making technology more legible, emotionally intuitive, and human-centered. We are building the foundation for a new generation of robots designed for everyday environments.

What to expect

In this role, you will be responsible for building the robotics hardware systems that power robot expression, communication, and behavior. You will work closely with ML/software engineers to build real-time robotics systems, and integrate robotic hardware with machine learning — turning research and simulation into reliable, production-ready robots.

In this role, you will:

- Develop robotic hardware that physically expresses perception, intelligence, and behavior

- Build robotic hardware that supports tasks such as computer vision, audio processing, and interaction understanding

- Integrate ML systems with robotic hardware and embedded systems

- Improve robot perception, responsiveness, and expression

- Collaborate with ML/software engineers to build expressive robotics systems

- Have strong CAD skills using tools such as Onshape, SolidWorks, Fusion360, or similar, as well as proficiency in 3D printing

- Have experience with human computer interaction as it relates to robots, especially robots in the home

- Are comfortable jumping into unfamiliar systems and can create order through chaos.

- Care about users and feel ownership over outcomes, even for systems you don't own.

- Think holistically about systems and approach complex problems with creative, outside-the-box solutions.

- Are passionate about building and experimenting with hardware

- Take ownership over the systems they design and build.

- Are curious, resourceful, and motivated to solve difficult problems.

- Work well in small, collaborative teams.

- Consider not just what immediately works, but how consumers will engage with robots.

Overview

Keysight is on the forefront of technology innovation, delivering breakthroughs and trusted insights in electronic design, simulation, prototyping, test, manufacturing, and optimization. Our ~15,000 employees create world-class solutions in communications, 5G, automotive, energy, quantum, aerospace, defense, and semiconductor markets for customers in over 100 countries.

Our powerful, award-winning culture embraces a bold vision of where technology can take us and a passion for tackling challenging problems with industry-first solutions. Diversity, equity & inclusion are integral parts of our culture and drivers of innovation at Keysight. We believe that when people feel a sense of belonging, they can be more creative, innovative, and thrive at all points in their careers.

Responsibilities

Looking for a challenging position in software development? Come join Keysight for a summer internship in Colorado Springs and help us build AI-powered features into the digital measurement instruments engineers depend on. You'll learn how to apply your engineering coursework and knowledge in software development to solve real-world problems.

About the Job

You will be part of an Agile software development team and will work on the design, implementation, and testing of AI-powered software features for Keysight digital instruments, including sampling and realtime oscilloscopes, BERTs, and AWGs. You will be assigned a self-contained project at the start of your internship, chosen from the team’s active work so that it delivers something the team keeps using after you leave. Projects span the range of what the team builds: applying AI and machine learning models to measurement problems, building agentic and LLM-based features, and creating the test and evaluation tooling those features need. This internship is a deliberate pipeline into our full-time R&D Engineer openings.

About the Team

We are not a research group: everything we build is aimed at shipping into products engineers depend on, working alongside the product teams that own those roadmaps. The team has a mix of new and experienced developers with a broad range of skills, and is eager to help you succeed. You will be paired with a mentor on the team and will report to the engineering manager, with regular guidance from the Solutions Architect.

Responsibilities

- Designing, implementing, testing, and documenting software for a scoped project on the team’s roadmap
- Applying Generative AI and agentic techniques, including prompt engineering, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), tool and function calling, and multi-step reasoning, under the direction of your mentor
- Writing automated tests and contributing to how we measure AI feature quality: test data sets, regression suites, and evaluation criteria for behavior that is not strictly deterministic
- Learning new development tools and processes, and working in the team’s Git, code review, and CI/CD practices
- Learning how the software in Keysight digital instruments works, and enough of the measurement domain to make sensible engineering decisions
- Participating in team stand-ups, design reviews, and demos, and communicating progress and blockers clearly
- Presenting your project and results to the team and to R&D leadership at the end of the internship

Qualifications

- Pursuing a BS in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Data Science, or an equivalent degree, with an expected graduation date between December 2027 and June 2028 (typically a rising senior)
- Experience with software development, source control, and testing
- Experience with object-oriented programming in a modern language such as Python, C++, C#, Rust, or Java, and the ability to write and debug non-trivial code independently
- Exposure to AI or machine learning concepts through coursework, personal projects, or prior internship work, plus clear curiosity about how AI-powered software is actually built
- Strong written and verbal communication, and the ability to work on-site in Colorado Springs for the duration of the internship
- Authorized to work in the United States without the need for employer-sponsored work authorization now or in the future

Desired Qualifications

- Hands-on experience with LLM APIs, RAG pipelines, or agentic frameworks such as LangGraph, AutoGen, CrewAI, or Semantic Kernel; coursework, hackathon, or side-project scale is fine
- Familiarity with Microsoft Visual Studio or Visual Studio Code
- Familiarity with Git source control
- Familiarity with Atlassian tools – Confluence, Jira, Bitbucket
- Coursework in signals and systems, digital signal processing, or communications, or any hands-on exposure to test and measurement instruments such as oscilloscopes, BERTs, or AWGs
- Experience building test automation or evaluation tooling of any kind
- Exposure to data analysis or ML libraries (NumPy, pandas, PyTorch, scikit-learn) or to running models on edge or embedded platforms
- Prior internship, co-op, research, or substantial open-source contribution experience
- Interest in returning for a full-time role after graduation

This is a paid, full-time internship of approximately 12 weeks, based on-site at Keysight’s Colorado Springs, Colorado facility. On-site presence is required for access to instrument hardware and measurement lab facilities. Start and end dates are flexible around your academic calendar.

SCOPE OF WORK:

The Children’s Legal Services (CLS) Legal Intern will support CLS attorneys in providing services to unaccompanied youth who entered the U.S. without a parent or legal guardian and who face deportation/removal in immigration court proceedings.

The legal intern will work under the supervision of CLS attorneys on specific projects to provide legal and factual research and analysis to support clients’ applications for Asylum, Special Immigrant Juvenile Status (SIJS), and other humanitarian forms of relief such as T and U visa applications for survivors of human trafficking and other serious crimes. The legal intern will have an opportunity to assist attorneys in preparing for immigration court hearings and/or state court custody/guardianship proceedings relevant to Special Immigrant Juvenile Status. In addition, the legal intern will have direct client interactions to support clients with initial screenings, follow-up meetings, drafting their declarations, gathering and preparing other evidence relevant to their immigration applications. The intern will perform clerical and administrative duties to ensure client notes are current and files are organized and kept up to date.

RESPONSIBILITIES

- Client interviews, follow-up meetings and client communications.
- Factual, Legal Research and Analysis. Intern will engage in fact-finding including country conditions factual research, legal research and analysis of client cases.
- Preparation of Testimony. Intern may assist client with initial drafting of their personal declarations and other personal fact-finding relevant to their immigration applications.
- Draft immigration applications and legal cover letters/briefs and court motions.
- Assist staff with monitoring status of clients’ immigration court removal proceedings
- Record client notes in case management system and assist legal staff with sorting, scanning and filing documents in case files.
- Adhere to IRC policies, particularly those related to confidentiality and client privacy.
- Display sensitivity to cultural and personality differences of clients. Respect their beliefs and values.
- Other related duties as assigned.

LEARNING OBJECTIVES:

- Intern will learn about U.S. immigration law in the context of unaccompanied minors and youth.
- Intern will develop problem solving and client services skills
- Intern will learn how to manage client cases within established deadlines

- Minimum 15 hours or up to 37.5 per week; preference for those that can work 37.5 hours.
- Must be currently enrolled in an accredited JD or LLM program.
- Spanish language proficiency is a plus but is not required.
- Strong desire to help immigrant youth in Maryland
- Ability to work independently, exercise good judgment, and have high attention to detail.
- Competency in Microsoft Office, data tracking, and file management
- Effective communication skills.
- Demonstrated ability to work effectively in a multicultural environment.
- Patience, understanding, flexibility, and a positive attitude.
- Willingness to learn about IRC history, philosophy, global work, and local efforts.
- Adherence to IRC code of conduct, volunteer and workplace policies

Join the New Product Development team for a hands-on engineering internship focused on automated test solutions for complex digital, analog, and mixed-signal integrated circuits used in automotive and industrial applications. - Analyze test and characterization data to investigate design margins, wafer-fabrication process variation, parametric performance, yield, and test-time opportunities.

- Contribute to ATE test hardware, socket design, board schematics, layout, diagnostic code, and test automation specifications under the guidance of experienced engineers.

- Document gaps, lessons learned, and best practices, and contribute reusable methods to the Standard Test Methods Library (STML) across ATE platforms.

- Language Fluency - English (Written & Verbal)

- Ability to work at least 40 hours per week during the internship.

- Prior related internship or co-op experience

- Demonstrated prior leadership experience in the workplace, school projects, competitions, etc.

- Strong interest in leveraging AI tools and emerging technologies to enhance productivity, streamline workflows, and support effective decision-making.

- Project management skills, i.e., the ability to innovate and execute on solutions that matter; the ability to navigate ambiguity.

- Strong written and verbal communication skills

- Strong planning & organizational skills

- Coursework or project experience in semiconductor test, design-for-test, integrated-circuit design, electronics, or semiconductor physics.

At Bose Corporation, we believe sound is the most powerful force on earth — and for over 60 years, we have been a company built on innovation, excellence, and independence. Privately owned, fiercely customer-focused, and driven by our values, we continue to lead industries and transform lives through sound.

Today, Bose Corporation is entering an exciting new era. Across multiple global Business Units and Global Functions, we are shaping the future of audio technology, automotive, luxury, and premium experiences. We invite you to join us in this transformation.

Job Description

ABOUT THE CO-OP PROGRAM

Bose Corporation is seeking students to participate in our Co-op Program who share our belief that sound is power. During the six-month co-op, students will have the chance to apply classroom learning in a hands-on work environment. Co-op participants will network across the business to gain diverse perspectives within Bose Corporation. Additionally, co-ops will connect with other students and colleagues, building valuable professional relationships for the future.

Spring Co-op: Candidates must be available to work full-time (40 hours per week) in a hybrid, in-office format from January through July, 2027. No relocation assistance is available.

THE ROLE

At Bose, we use machine learning across a diverse set of problems ranging from speech enhancement (e.g., SpeechClarity) to audio perception. As an Embedded Audio ML Engineer Co-op at Bose, you will help deploy and optimize our next generation deep learning algorithms for resource-constrained devices.

Responsibilities

- Build embedded software prototypes to demonstrate new ML-powered audio features on our wearables
- Design, implement, deploy and optimize deep learning models, data structure and algorithms on resource-constrained devices.
- Research, design and implement novel methods for efficient deep learning (e.g., quantization, pruning, NAS, knowledge distillation) with a focus on audio-related problems.
- Train and evaluate deep learning models to enable new experiences on our headphones, earbuds, soundbars, portable speakers and other consumer audio devices.
- Evaluate neural network hardware accelerators for low-power wearable devices, including working with various vendors’ custom toolchains, software and hardware and informing leadership teams about tradeoffs.

Minimum Qualifications

- Currently pursuing a M.S. or Ph.D. in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Machine Learning, or a related field
- Strong proficiency in C/C++ for embedded systems.
- Proficiency in Python for model conversion, evaluation, or tooling workflows.
- Strong experience implementing deep neural networks with PyTorch, TensorFlow, or similar frameworks
- Proven cross-group and cross-culture collaboration skills
- Creative problem-solver with demonstrated ability to work independently

Preferred Qualifications

- Prior internship or work experience as a Software/ML engineer
- Experience deploying ML models on edge or resource‑constrained devices (MCU/DSP/NPU).
- Solid background in audio deep learning and digital signal processing

Join the team bringing autonomy to the built world

At Bedrock, we're moving AI out of the lab and onto real job sites. Our team includes veterans who helped launch Waymo, scaled Segment to a $3.2B acquisition, and grew Uber Freight to $5B in revenue. We retrofit the heavy equipment contractors already own, starting with excavators, so experienced crews can safely take on more projects and deliver more of the critical infrastructure our society needs.

In August 2026, Bedrock-equipped excavators began doing fully autonomous, paid work on live commercial job sites. We've more than doubled our customer base since 2025, and our machines now work with contractors across the South, Midwest, and Mid-Atlantic

In October 2026, we raised a $600M Series C co-led by CapitalG and Emergence Capital, bringing our total funding to nearly $1B. We're using it to put more autonomous machines to work, build the field and operations teams behind every deployment, and expand into new machine types and job-site tasks.

This is where algorithms meet steel-toed boots. You'll work alongside construction veterans and world-class engineers to solve physical-world problems that simulations can't touch. If you're ready to do meaningful work on hard problems, we'd love to have you join us.

About the Role & Team

Before an autonomous excavator digs its first trench on a new site, it's already dug thousands in simulation. The Simulation team builds the virtual environments our autonomy stack trains and tests against — and the closer sim looks and behaves like the real world, the faster we move. Neural rendering is the next step: replacing hand-authored assets and approximations with learned representations that capture the visual complexity of real jobsites — dust, lighting, deformable terrain, heavy equipment in motion. As our Simulation intern, you'll push neural rendering techniques into our sim pipeline and measure whether they actually close the visual gap that matters for downstream autonomy performance.

What You'll Do

- Research, implement, and benchmark neural rendering methods (NeRF, 3D Gaussian splatting, or related techniques) for generating realistic construction-site imagery within our simulation stack

- Train models on real-world site data captured by our fleet and evaluate visual fidelity, temporal consistency, and render speed

- Integrate neural rendering outputs into the simulation pipeline so perception and planning teams can train and test against them

- Build evaluation metrics and tooling that quantify how well rendered scenes match real fleet data — and whether that improvement transfers to autonomy performance

- Identify and address failure modes: dynamic objects, deformable terrain, dust, harsh lighting, and other construction-specific challenges

- Document findings, limitations, and a recommendation on where neural rendering should (and shouldn't) replace traditional sim assets

What We're Looking For

Required

- Currently pursuing a BS, MS, or PhD in computer science, computer graphics, robotics, or a related field — or bringing equivalent research or industry experience

- Strong Python and hands-on experience with PyTorch (or equivalent)

- Solid understanding of 3D graphics fundamentals: rendering pipelines, scene representations, camera models, and coordinate systems

- Familiarity with neural scene representations (NeRF, Gaussian splatting, neural radiance fields, or related methods)

- Comfort with real-world data — construction sites are messy, dusty, and nothing like an indoor dataset

Preferred

- Published work or substantial project experience in neural rendering, novel view synthesis, or differentiable rendering

- Experience with simulation engines (Unreal, Unity, NVIDIA Isaac Sim, or similar)

- Background in autonomous vehicle simulation or synthetic data generation

- Familiarity with C++ and GPU programming (CUDA, OpenGL, Vulkan)

About This Internship

This is a fixed-term, project-based internship designed strictly for students (undergraduate or graduate) seeking resume-building experience, hands-on skill development, or industry exposure rather than a direct career launchpad. Candidates will own discrete, short-term projects that can be fully completed within the internship timeframe. Please note that while exceptional interns may occasionally be considered if business needs align, opportunities for full-time conversion are highly limited."

At Toyota Research Institute (TRI), we’re on a mission to improve the quality of human life. We’re developing new tools and capabilities to amplify the human experience. To lead this transformative shift in mobility, we’ve built a world-class team advancing the state of the art in AI, robotics, driving, and material sciences.

This is a paid 12-week internship opportunity and is a hybrid, in-office role.

Here’s a glimpse into the Internship experience from some of our TRI interns!

The Team

The World Foundation Models (WFM) team in the Robotics division is looking for research interns for the summer of 2027 in a variety of areas such as Video Generation, World Modeling, World-Action Models, 4D Reconstruction, Learning from Egocentric Videos, Multi-Modal Foundation Models, Multi-View Geometry, and Data Augmentation, with a primary focus on on embodied applications. We are aiming to make progress on some of the hardest scientific challenges around the deployment of robots in unstructured environments, by leveraging data from different sources and modalities, and learning transferable priors grounded in physical properties found in the real-world. Our mission is to develop foundational models capable of understanding how the world works, and in doing so predict possible future states from available information and adapt to new environments and circumstances.

The Internship

As a Research Intern, you will work with a multidisciplinary team proposing, conducting, and transferring pioneering research on the intersection between Computer Vision and Robotics. You will use large amounts of data from different sources and modalities, and train large-scale foundation models aimed at solving open problems, work towards publications at top academic venues, and test your ideas in simulators as well as in the real world.

Responsibilities

- Conduct daring research in Computer Vision that solves open problems of high theoretical and practical value, and evaluate solutions on real-world benchmarks and systems, with a focus on robotics.

- Push the boundaries of knowledge and the state-of-the-art in Visual Systems for Robotics.

- Partner with a multidisciplinary team, including other research scientists and engineers across the WFM team, the Robotics division, TRI, Toyota, and our university partners.

- Stay up to date on state-of-the-art Machine Learning ideas and software.

- Present results in verbal and written communications at international conferences, internally, and via open-source contributions to the community.

Qualifications

- Currently pursuing a Ph.D. in Machine Learning, Robotics, or related fields.

- Publication or desire to publish at high-impact conferences/journals (e.g., CoRL, ICLR, NeurIPS, CVPR, ICCV, ECCV, ICML, UAI, AISTATS, AAAI, TMLR, RSS, ICRA, IROS, RA-L, etc.) on some of the aforementioned topics.

- Passionate about large scale challenges in ML and CV grounded in physical systems, especially in the space of robotics.

Working at NLR

NLR is located at the foothills of the Rocky Mountains in Golden, Colorado is the nation's primary laboratory for energy systems research and development.

Join the National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR), where world-class scientists, engineers, and experts are accelerating energy innovation through breakthrough research and systems integration. From our mission to our collaborative culture, NLR stands out in the research community for its commitment to an affordable and secure energy future. Spanning foundational science to applied systems engineering and analysis, we focus on solving complex challenges to deliver advanced, secure, reliable, and cost-effective energy solutions. Our work helps strengthen U.S. industries, support job creation, and promote national economic growth.

At NLR, you'll find a mission-driven environment supported by state-of-the-art facilities, multidisciplinary research teams, and strong collaborations with industry, academia, and other national laboratories. We offer robust professional development opportunities, and a competitive benefits package designed to support your career and well-being.

Job Description

National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR) bridges research with real-world applications to advance new energy materials and technologies that lower costs, boost the economy, strengthen security, and deliver abundant and reliable energy. The Integrated Carbon Conversion Processes Group within NLR’s Catalytic Carbon Transformation and Scale-Up Center is seeking an Intern to provide researchers within our group the support necessary to achieve their cutting-edge research safely. . Our group’s mission is to de-risk and accelerate the scale-up of technologies for producing chemicals, fertilizers, and critical minerals from domestic biomass resources and waste resources. Our multidisciplinary team integrates expertise in process engineering, process science, catalysis, and computational modeling of integrated processes to translate laboratory discoveries into technically and economically viable processes suitable for pilot-scale demonstration and eventual commercialization. The directorate’s research encompasses multiple areas including analysis & characterization, biochemical processes, downstream processing, bioenergetics, and thermochemical processes.

Our research group is focused on developing chemicals, critical minerals, fertilizers, and materials from terrestrial and algal biomass. Our team brings together a wide range of technical expertise and global experience unified by a passionate drive to increase the technoeconomic feasibility and global adoption of biorefineries. Interdisciplinary collaboration and a relentless pursuit of advancing understanding at the intersection of fundamental science and industrial application is paramount to every member of our team.

The successful candidate will perform hands-on tasks and experimentation in a laboratory setting including the following:

- Batch and flow reactor operation for algal pretreatment, conversion, chemical production and polymer synthesis
- Develop renewable polyurethane materials for a broad range of applications.
- Benchtop wet chemistry, including sample preparation and derivatization,
- Operation and maintenance of analytical instrumentation, (e.g. FTIR, NMR, TGA, DSC, GC-MS, etc.)
- Separations, including liquid-liquid and solid-liquid extractions.
- Bioprocessing scale-up

The ability to conduct laboratory experiments and follow written procedures, with minimal supervision and with the utmost regard to safety is required. Self-motivation, adaptability and an aptitude for learning are critical for this role.

This is an excellent opportunity for a student invested in the NLR mission who desires relevant laboratory experience in preparation for graduate school or a career in the chemical industries.

Degree in Chemistry, Chemical Engineering, Biological Systems Engineering, Polymer Chemistry, or related discipline.

DriveTime Family of Brands is the largest privately owned used car sales finance & servicing company in the nation. You can find us at the intersection of technology and innovation as we use our proprietary tools and over two decades of industry knowledge to redefine the process of purchasing, financing, and protecting your vehicle.

That’s Nice, But What’s the Job?

We are looking for a skilled Software Engineering intern for our Summer 2027 internship program. - Work on business-critical projects built around cutting-edge technologies

- Intellectual curiosity. Why? What? How? Do you find yourself always wanting to learn more and broaden your knowledge base? If so, this could be the role for you.
- Plays well with others. You will be working in a high-functioning team environment. We work together in order to win together.
- Rebel with a cause. You are always looking beyond the obvious for continuous improvement.

- You are currently pursuing a bachelor's or master’s with a graduation date of December 2027 – May 2028

- Degree in Information Technology, computer science, or related field

- Strong problem-solving skills
- Understanding of HTML, CSS, JavaScript/ TypeScript, Python, Node.js, Java, GraphQL, C#, .NET and Azure

Anything Else? Absolutely.

DriveTime Family of Brands is Great Place to Work Certified! And get this: 90% of our rockstar employees say they feel right at home here. We could spend a lot of time having you read about ALL our awards, but we’ll save time (and practice some humility) just naming a few others; Comparably Awards: Best Company for Diversity, Best Company Culture and Best Company Leadership, oh and don’t forget Phoenix Business Journal Healthiest Employers (okay, we’ll stop there)!

Hiring is contingent upon successful completion of our background and drug screening process. DriveTime is a drug-free, tobacco-free workplace and an Equal Opportunity Employer.

And when it comes to hiring, we don't just look for the right person for the job, we seek out the right person for DriveTime. Buckle up for plenty of opportunities to grow in a professional, fun, and high-energy environment!

The Nuclear Company is the fastest growing AI tech-startup in the nuclear and energy space, pioneering a fleet-scale approach to building the next generation of nuclear reactors. Through our design-once, build-many model, we're accelerating the deployment of safe, reliable, and affordable nuclear energy.

We operate with an AI-first mindset. Every employee is expected to leverage AI, technology, and the Nuclear Operating System (NOS) as integral components of their role to improve the quality, speed, and impact of their work. We expect every team member to continuously identify opportunities to automate workflows, enhance decision-making, improve processes, and contribute to the ongoing evolution of NOS as a strategic operating capability that enables The Nuclear Company to scale with excellence.

We hire people who are driven by purpose, thrive in ambiguity, and are energized by building what has never been built before. Our team combines intellectual curiosity with high agency, embraces candid feedback and continuous learning, and holds themselves and others to exceptional standards. Our values—Trust, Responsibility, Unity, Scrappiness, and Tenacity—guide how we hire, collaborate, and make decisions every day. They are not words on a wall; they are the standard by which we operate. Trust is the foundation of our safety culture, fostering intellectual honesty, accountability, and open communication, while our values challenge every team member to execute with urgency, humility, resilience, and an unwavering commitment to our mission.

About the role

The United States is building nuclear power again, and The Nuclear Company is writing the software that makes it possible. NOS, the Nuclear Operating System, runs the regulatory, supply chain, cost, schedule, and field work behind real reactor construction. The work matters for national security, energy independence, and the climate.

You will build the AI that people use to build power plants. As an AI/ML Engineer Intern on the Platform Integration & AI/Data squad, you take real scope on the machine learning and agent capabilities inside NOS: LLM-driven workflows, retrieval-augmented generation, and agents that operate against NOS data and tools, plus the evals and monitoring that keep AI features safe in production. You work next to full-time engineers and nuclear domain experts, ship real models and features to production, and see your work put to use by the teams building plants.

This is a six-month co-op available in the Spring 2027 (January to June), aligned to the academic calendar. Base location is Washington DC, on-site five days a week, with full housing and relocation for co-ops outside the DC metro area.

Responsibilities

- Ship ML and AI features inside NOS applications teams use every day: site evaluation, red flag analysis, scheduling, lessons learned, and the stakeholder and project tools running across active TNC projects.

- Build AI agents and agent workflows that operate against NOS data and tools, including the MCP interfaces and tool-use frameworks they depend on.

- Develop data pipelines and integrations across Palantir Foundry, AWS GovCloud, and more — and contribute to the data ontology so models and agents can use NOS data reliably.

- Build predictive and anomaly-detection models that support operations and engineering decisions, including time-series analysis of sensor and operational data from active projects.

As a research intern in Keysight's Advanced Technology Laboratories, you will work on photonic integrated circuit (PIC) characterization and analysis using automated state-of-the-art instrumentation in a well-equipped laboratory. The successful candidate will possess a theoretical understanding and practical skills in photonic integrated circuits (PICs).

- Completed a B.S. degree in an engineering or science discipline
- Graduate student* majoring in Optics, Photonics, Physics, or Electrical Engineering
- Strong familiarity with PICs including:

- Integrated waveguide types and their properties
- Common fiber-to-chip coupling techniques and related components (optical I/O)
- Passive components (directional couplers, polarization splitters, rings, MMI’s, etc.)
- Active components (photodetectors, modulators, heaters, lasers, etc.)

- Python programming skills and familiarity with engineering packages (Numpy, Matplotlib, etc.)
- Experience in PIC component simulation, modeling and design
- Strong written and verbal English communication skills
- Self-motivated with an ability to work collaboratively in a multi-disciplinary team

- Lab automation – instrument control, data acquisition and motion control
- Familiarity with integrated photonic chip handling techniques
- Experience in PIC layout and GDS file handling
- Noise and signal analysis experience
- Familiarity with inverse design, agentic design, or data analytics

About the Organization

The Analytical Engineering Lab applies scientific and engineering methods to investigate product escalations, perform physical and root-cause analysis, and address unique or complex technical issues. The team drives product reliability through proactive risk mitigation across the product lifecycle from concept and development through production and end of life.

Role Overview

As a member of the Analytical Engineering Lab, you will support the analysis, testing, validation, and reliability assessment of electrical and electronic components, subsystems, and hardware systems. You will work with experienced engineers and internal and external development partners to identify risks, evaluate product performance, and develop reliable, cost-effective, and high-quality solutions.

Key Responsibilities

- Analyze electrical and electronic components, subsystems, integrated circuits, and related algorithms using established engineering principles, specifications, and requirements.
- Execute established test plans for existing and new designs.
- Support validation of: Electrical tolerances, form, fit, and function, shock and vibration performance, electromagnetic interference and emissions, product safety, reliability and durability, thermal performance, system power consumption and electrical characteristics.
- Assist with physical and root-cause analysis of electrical hardware issues, product escalations, and unique technical problems.
- Evaluate the reliability of materials, components, designs, and manufacturing techniques.
- Develop an understanding of electrical hardware design and development processes.
- Collaborate with internal engineering teams and outsourced development partners.
- Contribute as a member of cross-functional project teams to develop reliable, cost-effective, and high-quality solutions for low- to moderately complex products.
- Document analysis, test results, findings, and recommendations in clear technical reports and presentations.
- Provide technical support for design validation, reliability assessments, and proactive risk mitigation activities.

Required Education and Experience

- Currently enrolled in a bachelor’s degree program in Electrical Engineering, preferably with at least three years completed; or
- Currently enrolled in a master’s degree program in Electrical Engineering.

Required Knowledge and Skills

- Basic experience with or understanding of electrical design tools, simulation tools, and engineering software.
- Strong analytical, troubleshooting, and problem-solving skills.
- Understanding of electrical and electronic component design, integrated circuits, and hardware systems.
- Familiarity with electrical testing, measurement equipment, and engineering test methods.
- Understanding of thermal and electromagnetic properties of materials and methods for managing electromagnetic emissions.
- Ability to interpret engineering specifications, requirements, schematics, and test data.
- Strong written and verbal communication skills.
- Proficiency in English and the applicable local language, where required.
- Ability to work effectively both independently and as part of a technical project team.

Preferred Qualifications

- Coursework or project experience in electrical design, electronics, signal integrity, power systems, thermal analysis, electromagnetic compatibility, or reliability engineering.
- Experience using laboratory equipment such as oscilloscopes, multimeters, power supplies, electronic loads, spectrum analyzers, or network analyzers.
- Familiarity with root-cause analysis, design verification, validation testing, or reliability testing.
- Experience analyzing test data using tools such as MATLAB, Python, Excel, or similar software.

Docusign brings agreements to life. Over 1.5 million customers and more than a billion people in over 180 countries use Docusign solutions to accelerate the process of doing business and simplify people’s lives. With intelligent agreement management, Docusign unleashes business-critical data that is trapped inside of documents. Until now, these were disconnected from business systems of record, costing businesses time, money, and opportunity. The Observability Engineering team within Cloud & Production Engineering builds and operates the platforms that provide real-time visibility into the health, performance, and reliability of Docusign services. You will also contribute to the services that move this data reliably through the observability platform.

You will collaborate with engineers across infrastructure and product teams to improve how operational data is collected, processed, and exposed so teams can monitor, troubleshoot, and optimize their systems at scale. During the internship, you will work with a mentor and teammates to deliver and demonstrate a scoped 12-week project focused on telemetry pipelines, platform scale, or service reliability.

About us

Sierra is the leading platform for customer-facing AI agents, working with many of the world's biggest brands — including The GAP, Rocket Mortgage, SoFi, Sutter Health, and SoftBank — to transform how they serve customers and grow their businesses. We are primarily an in-person company based in San Francisco, with growing offices across North America, Europe, and Asia.

We are guided by a set of values that are at the core of our actions and define our culture: Trust, Customer Obsession, Craftsmanship, Intensity, and a commitment to balancing Family along the way. These values are the foundation of our work, and we are committed to upholding them in everything we do.

Our co-founders are Bret Taylor and Clay Bavor. Bret currently serves as Board Chair of OpenAI. Previously, he was co-CEO of Salesforce (which had acquired the company he founded, Quip) and CTO of Facebook. Bret was also one of Google's earliest product managers and co-creator of Google Maps. Before founding Sierra, Clay spent 18 years at Google, where he most recently led Google Labs. Earlier, he started and led Google’s AR/VR effort, Project Starline, and Google Lens. Before that, Clay led the product and design teams for Google Workspace.

Program overview

- APX is Sierra’s rotational program to develop the next generation of AI builders.

- In the age of AI, we believe generalists with diverse training and experience will become more important and empowered than ever. Instead of specializing early in an engineering, product management, or business subfield, the next generation of AI leaders will be able to do everything it takes to create, ship, and distribute great products.

- As an APX, you’ll be among the first to live in this exciting future. You’ll build AI agents directly with top global brands and gain access to comprehensive training opportunities and rotations across our Agent Development and Core Product teams. If you’re hungry to shape the most important technological wave of our lifetimes, come build at Sierra.

- The APX program is open to students graduating from undergraduate or Master’s programs by June 2027.

What you’ll do

- Build and ship AI agents with Sierra’s customers in a fast-paced, production environment.

- Contribute directly to Sierra’s platform by writing code and designing products.

- Learn how we build agents that operate at scale and evolve through real-world usage.

- Collaborate closely with engineers, product managers, and operators across the company.

- Participate in internal reviews and product discussions to push the boundaries of what agents can do.

What you'll bring

- Pursuing a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree (or comparable program) in Computer Science or a related field.

- Professional experience in software engineering or product management, especially with customer-facing responsibilities.

- Expertise in React, TypeScript, Python, Go, and other modern programming languages.

- Demonstrated curiosity and interest in AI applications (e.g., research, jobs, side projects).

Our values

- Trust: We build trust with our customers with our accountability, empathy, quality, and responsiveness. We build trust in AI by making it more accessible, safe, and useful. We build trust with each other by showing up for each other professionally and personally, creating an environment that enables all of us to do our best work.

- Customer Obsession: We deeply understand our customers’ business goals and relentlessly focus on driving outcomes, not just technical milestones. Everyone at the company knows and spends time with our customers. When our customer is having an issue, we drop everything and fix it.

- Craftsmanship: We get the details right, from the words on the page to the system architecture. We have good taste. When we notice something isn’t right, we take the time to fix it. We are proud of the products we produce. We continuously self-reflect to continuously self-improve.

- Intensity: We know we don’t have the luxury of patience. We play to win. We care about our product being the best, and when it isn’t, we fix it. When we fail, we talk about it openly and without blame so we succeed the next time.

- Family: We know that balance and intensity are compatible, and we model it in our actions and processes. We are the best technology company for parents. We support and respect each other and celebrate each other’s personal and professional achievements.

What we offer

We want our benefits to reflect our values and offer the following to full-time employees:

- Flexible (unlimited) paid time off

- Medical, dental, and vision benefits for you and your family

- Life insurance and disability benefits

- Retirement plan dependent on country of employment

- Parental leave

- Fertility and family building benefits through Carrot

- Lunch, as well as delicious snacks and coffee to keep you energized

- Discretionary benefit stipend giving people the ability to spend where it matters most

- Free alphorn lessons

These benefits are further detailed in Sierra's policies, may vary by region, and are subject to change at any time, consistent with the terms of any applicable compensation or benefits plans. Eligible full-time employees can participate in Sierra's equity plans subject to the terms of the applicable plans and policies.

Be you, with us

We're working to bring the transformative power of AI to every organization in the world. To do so, it is important to us that the diversity of our employees represents the diversity of our customers. We believe that our work and culture are better when we encourage, support, and respect different skills and experiences represented within our team. - Have built something from scratch through a class, research project, internship, startup, open-source contribution, or personal project

Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

ABOUT THE TEAM

The Air Dominance and Strike Low Observable Team are advancing into the next generation of LO Technology to enhance the survivability and effectiveness of unmanned air systems. Our Low Observables engineering team is responsible for designing, analyzing, testing, and sustaining stealth features that reduce radar (RCS) and infrared (IR) signatures, ensuring our systems remain undetectable in contested environments.

ABOUT THE ROLE

This is an intern role open to engineers finishing a degree in aerospace, electrical, or mechanical engineering. Low Observables work sits at the intersection of all three: the shape of the air vehicle, the electromagnetic behavior of its surfaces, and the materials and processes used to build it.

You do not need prior stealth experience. Almost nobody arrives with it, because most of it cannot be taught outside a cleared program. We will teach you the LO-specific methods. What we are looking for is strong engineering fundamentals, comfort picking up unfamiliar analysis tools, and the judgment to tell a real result from a bad one.

You will be paired with an LO engineer and start on a scoped piece of a live program, not a training exercise.

WHAT YOU'LL DO:

- Run broadband Radar Cross Section (RCS) analysis on components and full air vehicles, and learn to judge when a prediction can be trusted

- Support the design and development of Low Observable unmanned air systems, from early configuration trades through detailed design

- Build and improve the analysis tools, scripts, and validation workflows the team runs on

- Model LO materials and treatments, and help select and optimize them for specific components

- Support manufacturing and validation planning, including tolerances, inspection methods, and what is actually producible at rate

- Help plan and execute RCS measurement campaigns in indoor chambers and on outdoor ranges, then reduce and interpret the data

- Compare measured results against predictions, chase down the disagreements, and feed what you learn back into the models

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

- Must be pursuing a bachelor’s or master’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a related field.

- Must be returning to school at the end of the internship to continue academic studies for at least one quarter or semester.

- Must be a U.S. Person due to required access to U.S. export-controlled information or facilities; U.S. clearance eligibility may be required depending on program.

- Ability to complete an in-person 12-week internship in one of our offices in summer 2027.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:

- Coursework in at least one of: electromagnetics or RF, aircraft or vehicle design, or materials and manufacturing processes

- Working knowledge of a scripting or analysis language such as MATLAB, Python, or C++

- Familiarity with a 3D CAD package such as NX, CATIA, SolidWorks, or Creo

- Demonstrated hands-on engineering work: a capstone or senior design project, internship, undergraduate research, or a student competition team

- Ability to explain a technical result clearly, in writing and in a design review

- Exposure to any electromagnetic simulation tool, such as HFSS, CST, FEKO, or COMSOL. X-Patch, SENTRi, and McMoM2D are government codes and we do not expect you to have used them

- Coursework or project experience with composites, additive manufacturing, casting, or injection molding

- Experience with laboratory RF measurement: network analyzers, anechoic chambers, or antenna pattern measurement

- Experience reducing, visualizing, and sanity-checking measured data sets

- A prior internship or co-op in aerospace, defense, or another hardware-heavy environment

About Didi Autonomous Driving

Founded in 2016, DiDi's autonomous driving unit is dedicated to developing Level 4 autonomous driving technology to make transportation safer, more efficient, and accessible. In 2019, the unit became an independent company, Voyager, to accelerate technology development, commercialization, and large-scale deployment. By combining DiDi's unique data advantage, operational expertise, and mobility ecosystem, we aim to build a reliable, scalable autonomous fleet that integrates seamlessly with human-driven services. Driven by real-world customer needs and a strong commitment to safety and user experience, our mission is to deliver autonomous mobility solutions that create meaningful value for riders and communities.

About the Role

We want our vehicles to understand the physical world as it is right now, instead of relying on a map drawn long ago. Roads change, and the world a car actually drives in is always more complex than any static record of it. We are seeking a Research Intern to help give our planner a more accurate and up-to-date picture of the world, so the vehicle handles complex real-world scenes more robustly. In this role, you will take on hard, open problems from real-world driving and solve them with frontier research methods. You will report directly to the team lead and work on the problem from definition to validated solution. Strong results will often be worth publishing, and we will support you in writing them up, but the goal is to solve problems that matter to the product.

Responsibilities

- Survey the latest research in scene understanding, prediction, and planning, and turn it into practical approaches that fit our system and constraints.

- Design and implement deep learning models that build a richer, real-time understanding of the driving environment from onboard sensors and other available sources.

- Train and evaluate models on large-scale data from our driving logs and on public benchmarks, and lead failure analysis to find out where and why models fall short.

- Define metrics and evaluation methods that connect perception quality to how the vehicle actually drives.

- Turn successful prototypes into solutions that work with our planning stack, with help from production engineers.

- Collaborate with Perception, Prediction, Planning, and Mapping teams so results move from experiment to product.

Qualifications

- Currently enrolled in an M.S. or Ph.D. program in Computer Science, Robotics, Electrical Engineering, Machine Learning, or a related field, for the full duration of the internship.

- Available for a full-time onsite internship of 3–6 months; start dates are flexible.

- Strong programming skills in Python, and experience with modern deep learning frameworks such as PyTorch or JAX.

- Hands-on experience designing, training, and debugging deep learning models for computer vision, 3D perception, or sequential decision-making.

- Solid understanding of autonomous driving fundamentals, including perception, prediction, and motion planning.

- Ability to read research critically, form hypotheses, and turn them into well-controlled experiments.

- Excellent communication and collaboration skills.

Preferred Qualifications

- Publications at top venues such as CVPR, ICCV, ECCV, NeurIPS, ICLR, ICML, ICRA, IROS, CoRL or IV.

- Experience with multi-modal sensor fusion (camera, lidar, radar) or BEV representations.

- Experience with transformers, graph neural networks, or other structured scene representations.

- Experience with uncertainty estimation, or with learning-based prediction or planning.

- Experience with large-scale model training and data pipelines.

- Experience with public autonomous driving datasets such as nuScenes, Argoverse 2, or the Waymo Open Dataset.

- Proficiency in C++ (CUDA is a plus) and experience with robotics systems.

The hourly rate for the Intern position in the selected city is $46.

About Zipline

Zipline is the world’s largest and most experienced drone delivery service. We are on a mission to serve all humans equally by ensuring access to food, medicine and essential goods anytime, anywhere. We design, build, and operate the world’s largest autonomous logistics system, delivering critical supplies quickly and reliably. Today, Zipline operates on four continents, makes a delivery somewhere in the world every 30 seconds, and has completed millions of deliveries to date, including blood, vaccines, medical supplies, food, and retail products.

Our customers include the world’s largest and most prominent healthcare systems, governments, retailers, restaurants and global businesses who rely on us to save lives, reduce emissions, increase economic opportunity, and provide delivery from point A to point B as fast as possible. The drone is only 15% of what we’ve built to enable seamless, reliable, global operations.

Our system strengthens supply chains, reduces congestion, and gives people time back. With more than 140 million commercial autonomous miles safely flown, Zipline is redefining access to healthcare, consumer products, and food across the globe.

We operate at a global scale and are looking for practical problem solvers who thrive on real-world challenges and rapid growth. Our team is motivated by building systems that have a direct, meaningful impact on people’s lives and by scaling the future of logistics. We are seeking people who sculpt from first principles, enjoy facing adversity, and can do the impossible at record breaking speeds.

About the Applied Aerodynamics Team

Without the Aerodynamics team, the Zipline drones would not fly! This team is responsible for the aerodynamic performance of the aircraft, from high-level aeronautical considerations down to the detailed surface design. We work on everything from the body and propellers to vehicle dynamics and aeroacoustics, and in order to ensure our product is successful we collaborate strongly with almost every other engineering team, including GNC, structures, mechanical integration, avionics, perception, systems, weather and others.

The Role

As an intern in the Aerodynamics Team you can expect to work on any one of our current open projects alongside our world-class aerodynamicists and aeronautical engineers, both learning from their experience and bringing your own perspective to the tasks. This is an opportunity to test the skills and knowledge you’ve learned at school in a practical and fast-paced environment, where we leverage our understanding of physics to solve real problems. You will learn to use a variety of tools - from low fidelity calculations, through CFD simulation to experimental analysis - to help drive the design of our current and future products forward.

What You'll Do

- Vehicle design analysis including aerodynamics, propulsion, and power system performance.

- Low- and high-fidelity analytical modeling of vehicle subsystems and behaviors

- Aerodynamic database generation and building analysis of flight behaviors

- Experiment planning, execution and data analysis, from wind tunnels to flight tests

- Support multidisciplinary team including controls, mechanical, production, software, and electrical engineers to tackle design challenges and resolve time-sensitive issues

What You'll Bring

- You will be studying one or more of the following areas: fluid mechanics, aerodynamics, flight physics, aeronautical engineering, acoustics. A strong understanding of the technical content of these courses is the most valuable asset you will bring, and will help you exercise good engineering judgment.

- Understanding and experience with any of the following toolsets is advantageous. If you have not used the tool before, we’ll teach you to use it where needed.

- Continuum- or Lattice Boltzmann-based computational fluid dynamics, such as STAR-CCM+, Fluent, OpenFOAM, or PowerFLOW

- Wind tunnel test identification, planning, execution, troubleshooting, and data analysis using a variety of electro-mechanical and optical diagnostic techniques

- Flight test planning for system identification and simulation validation, cross functional planning, test execution, and data analysis

- MATLAB, Python, Rust, or similar software tools

- CAD advanced surfacing tools, such as CATIA or NX

- To be maximally effective we will need you to work in our head office in South San Francisco. For certain testing programs, limited travel (within California) may be required.

What Else You Should Know

Our internships are full-time positions, in-person at our South San Francisco or Dallas office. We will host our Spring 2027 interns from January to April/May.

Candidates are limited to three (3) applications within a 30-day period.

The hourly rate for this internship is $48 per hour. On our proprietary research team—Market Intelligence—you’ll support Canvas team members as they work with our investment professionals and Compliance team to uncover insights about companies, industries, and the broader economy through deep fundamental research and applying data science and engineering techniques to alternative data sets. You’ll work alongside a talented team with diverse skills, backgrounds, and perspectives.

Canvas is the supply chain research group within Market Intelligence. Canvas conducts compliant supply chain research by developing deep industry expertise, talking with private company executives, and synthesizing information for portfolio managers and analysts. Our team produces impactful research that will change the way you look at the world.

When you join the Canvas team, you’re signing up for the learning experience of a lifetime. You will never look at anything the same way—from grocery stores to tires to semiconductors. Every day, Canvas team members speak with some of the most successful private company executives and learn about the businesses they’ve spent their lives building. The team synthesizes findings in comprehensive reports that are consumed by our investment professionals. Other Market Intelligence divisions conduct quantitative research to explain what is going on in an industry. As a Canvas Fundamental Researcher, our qualitative research helps explain why it is happening.

During the 10-week program based in our New York office, you will gain exposure to:

- How Canvas develops subject matter expertise across a range of industries

- Gathering insights from small, medium, and large private company executives into their businesses and the industries in which they operate, including real-time changes in supply/demand dynamics, emerging competitors, markets, and technologies

- Synthesizing research findings in comprehensive daily summaries and reports

- Business leaders across industries, collaborating with Canvas colleagues, and how Canvas research supports more informed investment decision making

- Work alongside your fellow interns and be mentored by experienced professionals

- Meet your peers through designated intern programming, volunteer opportunities, and social events

- Attend sessions with senior leaders discussing their expertise and career paths

- Get hands on access to the wealth of tools and resources that Point72 employees use every day

- Develop technical, writing, and presentation skills

- Participate in networking opportunities across the firm, with groups such as Trading, Finance, Trade Support, Compliance, and Technology

What’s Required

- Bachelor’s degree expected between Fall 2027 and Spring 2028

- Demonstrated academic success and strong analytical skills

- Excellent written and verbal communication abilities

- An eagerness to find out if your conclusions are right or wrong

- An interest in learning how companies work (processes and outcomes)

- Intellectual curiosity, creative thinking, and professional maturity

- Commitment to the highest ethical standards

Point72 is a leading global alternative investment firm led by Steven A. Cohen. About Zipline

Zipline is the world’s largest and most experienced drone delivery service. We are on a mission to serve all humans equally by ensuring access to food, medicine and essential goods anytime, anywhere. We design, build, and operate the world’s largest autonomous logistics system, delivering critical supplies quickly and reliably. Today, Zipline operates on four continents, makes a delivery somewhere in the world every 30 seconds, and has completed millions of deliveries to date, including blood, vaccines, medical supplies, food, and retail products.

Our customers include the world’s largest and most prominent healthcare systems, governments, retailers, restaurants and global businesses who rely on us to save lives, reduce emissions, increase economic opportunity, and provide delivery from point A to point B as fast as possible. The drone is only 15% of what we’ve built to enable seamless, reliable, global operations.

Our system strengthens supply chains, reduces congestion, and gives people time back. With more than 140 million commercial autonomous miles safely flown, Zipline is redefining access to healthcare, consumer products, and food across the globe.

We operate at a global scale and are looking for practical problem solvers who thrive on real-world challenges and rapid growth. Our team is motivated by building systems that have a direct, meaningful impact on people’s lives and by scaling the future of logistics. We are seeking people who sculpt from first principles, enjoy facing adversity, and can do the impossible at record breaking speeds.

About the System Validation Team

The System Validation Team ensures the performance, reliability, and safety of Zipline’s integrated system of systems, including the Zip, Droid, and Dock. We specialize in Hardware-in-the-Loop (HIL) testing, enabling us to validate complex interactions across hardware and software before real-world deployment. Our team builds and maintains automated pipelines that rigorously test software in a simulated environment, ensuring it meets high standards before being tested in flight. By catching potential issues early and refining system behavior, we play a critical role in delivering reliable, safe, and efficient solutions that power Zipline’s mission to transform global logistics. Our team owns automation of flight testing as well to capture issues before it happens in commercial flights.

The Role

As a System Validation Intern, you will contribute to testing and validating Zipline’s complete system of systems—spanning the Zip, Droid, and Dock. You’ll help build and refine automated testing pipelines, ensuring that software meets rigorous quality standards before being tested in flight. Working closely with a supportive and experienced team, you’ll develop hands-on experience with cutting-edge tools and technologies while solving meaningful challenges. Your work will play an essential role in ensuring the reliability of systems that deliver life-saving goods worldwide. This role offers a unique opportunity to learn, grow, and make an impact in a fast-paced, mission-driven environment.

What You'll Do

- Assist in executing Hardware-in-the-Loop (HIL) tests and flight tests to validate the interaction between Zipline’s Zip, Droid, and Dock systems.

- Collaborate with a wide range of engineers from different teams to build and refine automated pipelines that test software before it is deployed in flight.

- Design and improve tools that stress-test the system in off-nominal cases.

- Analyze and troubleshoot hardware and software issues uncovered during testing, contributing to system improvements.

- Work alongside a multidisciplinary team to design and execute system-level validation plans.

- Develop and enhance scripts and tools to support automated testing workflows.

- Learn how to ensure reliability and quality in complex, safety-critical systems, gaining valuable insights into real-world engineering challenges.

What You'll Bring

- You must have completed the second year of your undergraduate studies. Master's and PhD students are also eligible.

- Strong understanding of engineering design fundamentals and the ability to triage and identify root causes of technical issues.

- Experience writing Rust or Python scripts to automate tasks or tests, either through coursework or personal projects.

- Hands-on experience writing Python tests using tools like Pytest or Unittest.

- Familiarity with creating and executing test plans or validation plans for software or hardware systems.

- A hands-on approach to problem-solving, including debugging and triaging technical issues.

- General understanding of electrical systems such as motors, sensors, cameras, and onboard computers.

- Experience working in a Linux environment, including using command-line tools effectively.

- Familiarity with tools like Git for version control, bazel for build and test management and Jira for task tracking.

- Basic understanding of networking concepts such as RPC or sockets.

- Experience working with CI tools like GitHub Actions, Buildkite, or similar.

- Strong attention to detail and organizational skills to document test results and track issues effectively.

What Else You Should Know

This internship is a full-time position, in-person at our South San Francisco office. We will host our Spring 2027 interns from January to April.

The hourly rate for this internship is $40 per hour. Additional benefits may include relocation support, a housing stipend, overtime pay, paid sick time, and other benefits, where applicable and subject to local requirements.Zipline is an equal opportunity employer and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws or our own sensibilities.

Zipline is also committed to providing reasonable accommodations to individuals with disabilities. Please let your point of contact at Zipline know if you require any accommodations throughout your interview process.

Voluntary Self-Identification

For government reporting purposes, we ask candidates to respond to the below self-identification survey. Completion of the form is entirely voluntary. Whatever your decision, it will not be considered in the hiring process or thereafter. Any information that you do provide will be recorded and maintained in a confidential file.

As set forth in Zipline ’s Equal Employment Opportunity policy, we do not discriminate on the basis of any protected group status under any applicable law.

Job Description

The Role:

Global Manufacturing Electrical & SDV is seeking curious, driven students who want to be part of something bigger than themselves. If you're energized by real challenges, eager to learn, and ready to contribute to meaningful work that shapes the future of the automotive industry, this opportunity is for you.

This isn’t just about getting experience—it’s about making an impact. You’ll work alongside experienced professionals, gain hands-on exposure to cutting-edge projects, and see firsthand how your ideas can influence real-world outcomes. You’ll face fast-paced environments and evolving priorities, but you’ll also have the support of a people-first culture that values growth, learning, and balance.

If you're excited to build your skills, expand your perspective, and contribute to something with real purpose, we’d love to hear from you.

The Team:

Global Manufacturing Electrical & SDV helps GM build high-quality vehicles to our customers by combining electrical engineering, software, data, testing, and manufacturing expertise. Our team works to improve Electrical First-Time Quality, solve plant-critical challenges, and develop scalable solutions. We bring manufacturing software and hardware design in-house to move faster and enable Vehicle as a Tester (VaaT) and SDV 2.0 capabilities. Interns will gain hands-on experience solving real manufacturing problems and contributing to innovations that will shape the future of vehicle production.

As a student in the Global Manufacturing Electrical & SDV organization, you will focus on delivering innovative manufacturing solutions that help support electrical first-time quality (E-FTQ) at our plants. You will:

- Help drive meaningful progress in vehicle electrical systems through hands-on projects and problem-solving.

- Foster a forward-thinking work culture that embraces change and navigates future organizational and industry challenges.

- Build and nurture strategic relationships across various functions including software, manufacturing, and program management to synergize efforts towards future innovations.

Examples of past intern projects include:

- Assist with writing manufacturing software code (using C++) that supports the next generation of vehicle electrical systems.

- Build easy-to-understand dashboards using Power BI to help manufacturing and engineering teams make data-driven decisions and solve the customer and plants’ biggest problems.

- Help design innovative electrical tooling and equipment solutions that empower assembly plants to ensure the highest quality vehicle electrical systems and create the standardized work for use of this hardware.

- Designing and documenting a scalable test setup that provides shared power and network connections for vehicle electronic components.

Required Qualifications:

- Pursuit of a bachelor’s or master’s degree in engineering or technology in one of the following areas: Automotive, Computer/Computer Science/Computer Animation, Construction Management, Civil, Industrial, Industrial Operations, Information Technology, Machine Learning, Manufacturing, Mechanical, Mechatronics, Robotics, Software, Data Scientists, or equivalent field

- Must be graduating between December 2027 and June 2010

- Able to work fulltime, 40 hours per week during the summer months

- Insatiable curiosity and desire to learn

- Demonstrated leadership in academic, extracurricular, or project settings

- Conceptual understanding and/or experience in any of the following:

- Manufacturing processes

- Programming or understanding software logic (e.g., Linux, C++)

- Information Technology systems

- Ability to work independently and with a team

- Effective communication and relationship-building skills

- High level of integrity, self-motivation, and adaptability in a fast-paced environment

GM does not provide immigration-related sponsorship for this role. Do not apply for this role if you will need GM immigration sponsorship now or in the future.
